newsitem.title: USA: CSCE WORLD SUGAR SETTLES DOWN SLIGHTLY, TRADE SLIM.
newsitem.headline: CSCE WORLD SUGAR SETTLES DOWN SLIGHTLY, TRADE SLIM.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures closed a thinly-traded session barely lower and within the recent trading range.
Floor sources said commission house selling pressured prices from the outset, pushing the benchmark October contract to the day's low of 11.45 cents.
Trade interest supported the contract at the low of 11.45 cents and light local buying carried the spot month slightly over unchanged and to the day's high of 11.54 cents.

The market drifted in its nine-point trading range amid a dearth of inspiring fundamental news, market sources said, adding that the U.S. Department of Agriculture's forecasts for output in the 1997/98 marketing year had already been filtered into the market.
The USDA boosted its estimate of the total crop to 7.67 million short tons raw value, from its previous forecast.

U.S. sugar beet production was seen at 4.3 million short tons, unchanged from the July estimate. U.S. sugar cane production was pegged at 3.36 million short tons, up 2.7 percent from last month's estimate.
October closed unchanged at 11.53 cents a lb, having ranged from 11.53 to 11.45 cents. The rest of the board settled flat to 0.03 cent weaker.
Market sources expect October to test nearby resistance at 11.55 cents on Wednesday, and then pull back. Support was pegged at the recent low of 11.32 cents.
Firm resistance was seen at 11.87 cents, the recent high basis the October contract.
An estimated 7,598 lots changed hands on the day compared with Monday's official 12,742 lots.
